title: Module quiz: Integration choices, access and capability bloat

questions.stem: A team has 60 tools and turns on the tool search tool. A developer proposes to omit the least-used tools from the request, to save tokens. What does the documentation say?

options.text: Send the least-used ones inside the system prompt as plain text
options.says: Ruled out because deferral changes "what enters the context window", and text in the prompt would load them all every time.

options.text: Send only the loaded tools, and keep the rest in the application
options.says: Ruled out because "You still send every tool's full definition in the `tools` array on every request".

options.text: Send every definition and mark the infrequent ones as deferred
options.says: The search runs on the full set, so every definition is sent and the infrequent ones are marked as deferred.

options.text: Send every definition with a cache breakpoint on each deferred one
options.says: Ruled out because deferred tools are kept out of the prefix, and "A deferred tool cannot itself carry a cache breakpoint".

origin.section: Capability bloat, progressive discovery and the practice

questions.stem: A gateway receives a request whose credential has been revoked and which also names a model that the team may not use. What does it answer, and what does it record?

options.text: A refusal for the model, recorded under the team that owned the revoked credential
options.says: Ruled out because "A request with no credential is refused as unauthenticated even when it also asks for a model it may not have".

options.text: A refusal as unauthenticated, logged under unknown with the verdict but no prompt text
options.says: Who is calling comes first, and the record keeps "the team (or "unknown"), the model and the verdict, and no prompt text".

options.text: An approval with a warning in the log, since a revoked credential is the provider's concern
options.says: Ruled out because "every decision, the refusals included, leaves a record".

options.text: A refusal that keeps the full prompt in the record, so that an attack can be studied later
options.says: Ruled out because "a log of content is its own data-protection problem".

origin.section: A gateway: one place for credentials, limits and records

questions.stem: A partner company's autonomous research system, built on another framework, must hand sub-tasks to your own autonomous system and collect the results. Which mechanism does the integration use?

options.text: An MCP server that exposes your system as one tool of the partner's system
options.says: Ruled out because "MCP is for agent-to-tool communication", and the partner's agent is a peer and not a tool.

options.text: A direct call from the partner's code into the functions of your system
options.says: Ruled out because a direct call suits "The path is known: the same steps in the same order", and a delegation between two agents is not that.

options.text: A subagent that your own framework starts on the partner's behalf
options.says: Ruled out because A2A is "Not a sub-agent or tool-call protocol", and a subagent is how an agent delegates inside its own framework, not across two.

options.text: An agent-to-agent protocol between the two independent parties
options.says: The counterpart is an independent agent with its own owner, which is the agent-to-agent case.

origin.section: Which mechanism connects it, what a gateway centralises and whose rights a call uses
